title: Beta feature-flag rollout comms & Q&A (runtime cache pilot)
body:
Context:
- Small internal pilot to enable the new prefix-KV cache behavioral optimizations behind a feature flag for 10% of traffic on hosted-api. Goal: reduce p99 token latency and GPU token-cost by improving KV cache hit patterns for short-context assistants.

Audience:
- Primary: Eng (serving-runtime, infra), Product (hosted-api), SRE/observability, Support on-call.
- Secondary: Console, Solutions Eng for customer-facing FAQs.

High-level announcement (Slack / internal-mail draft) — SHORT:
- TL;DR: Starting Tues 02/25 we'll enable the "runtime-prefix-cache-v2" flag for 10% of hosted-api traffic in us-west. This is a controlled pilot to validate latency and cost improvements. Expect minor variance in tail latency for some long-context workloads — rollback plan in place. Please use #runtime-pilot for issues.

Longer announcement (all-hands/email format) — DRAFT:
- Subject: Pilot: runtime-prefix-cache-v2 feature flag (hosted-api)
- Body: Hey team — we’re kicking off a small pilot of the new prefix/KV caching behavior that adapts cache retention to conversation patterns. This aims to improve p99 generation latency for chat workloads and cut per-token GPU cost by ~6-12% in early tests. Pilot scope: 10% traffic, us-west, 48h initial observation window. Owners: Ryan (runtime), Aisha (observability), Noelle (product). Rollback automated at 15% error spike or sustained latency regressions (more below). Links: design doc + experiment dashboards.

Key talking points for sync / all-hands drop-in:
- Why this matters: small client-side changes + server caching logic can move unit economics materially — helps make Dedicated/private cost targets easier.
- Expected wins: reduce average token compute, p95/p99 latency improvements for short-turn dialogs, better KV hit reuse.
- Risks: rare increased latency for >8k context sequences; potential increased memory pressure in some GPU configs. We’ll monitor and cap cache size per instance.
- Rollout controls: gradual ramp, traffic sampling, automated guardrails, manual kill switch.

Planned rollout schedule (tentative):
- 02/25 08:00 UTC: Enable flag 1% -> dry-run metrics for 2h
- 02/25 10:00 UTC: If stable, increase to 10%
- 02/25 18:00 UTC: Evaluate 8-hour window; if met success metrics, keep at 10% for 48h
- 02/27 10:00 UTC: Decision point — scale to 25% or roll back

Success metrics (primary):
- p99 generation latency delta <= -6% (improvement)
- per-token GPU cycles reduced >= 4% across sampled models
- no increase in 5xx rate > 0.05% absolute

Guardrails / automated rollback triggers:
- 5xx spike > 0.05% OR
- sustained p99 increase > +10% for 30m OR
- memory pressure > 85% on any instance class for 10m
- Any of above triggers: automated rollback to previous flag state and pager to runtime oncall

Observability / dashboards to watch:
- Runtime/latency per-model (p50/p95/p99) — dashboard link in Confluence
- GPU utilization + memory by instance type
- Cache hit/miss ratio and average cache size per host
- Customer error logs + increase in degraded responses in the proxy layer

Owner & escalation map:
- Experiment owner: Noelle Martinez (product-hosted-api)
- Runtime lead: Ryan Park (eng-serving-runtime)
- Observability: Aisha Gupta (observability)
- SRE on-call: see #oncall rota
- Escalation: if automation fails, tag @ryan @aisha; for customer-impacting incidents, involve @tarun (support leader) and @ceo if outage > 30m

Q&A — anticipated questions + suggested replies (internal):
Q: Will this affect production customers?
A: Only a small fraction (10%) initially. We will proactively notify any customers who hit the pilot cohort if they report anomalies. No config change required on customer side.

Q: What models are in-scope?
A: Medium and small open models we serve most as part of hosted catalog (see linked experiment config); large models excluded for first run.

Q: How do we identify pilot traffic?
A: Sampled by routing layer using hashed request id + account bucketing. We will log cohort id on traces.

Q: Can we rollback quickly?
A: Yes — the flag flip is an atomic config change across the runtime pool. We have automated rollback triggers + manual kill switch in console. Expect <60s to revert in practice, with some in-flight requests completing.

Q: What should Support do if a user reports slow responses?
A: Open a ticket -> tag #runtime-pilot -> include request-id and timestamp. Support playbook: check cohort tag -> if in pilot, escalate to runtime oncall; if not, follow normal debugging.

Draft support message template (copyable):
- Thanks for flagging — we’re running a small pilot of a runtime cache behavior that may intermittently affect latency for a tiny subset of traffic. Could you share the request-id and timestamp? We’ll route to runtime immediately. Apologies for the disruption; we’ll revert if we see repeated issues.

Open TODOs (short):
- Finish dashboard panels: Aisha (by 02/24)
- Add cohort tag to trace logs: Ryan (PR #890)
- Draft customer-facing FAQ (if we scale): Noelle (w/ Solutions Eng)
- Run canary in staging w/ synthetic long-context traffic: Ethan (02/22)
- Review quota/ratelimit interactions with cache: Platform Eng (TBD)

Notes / scraps (things I want to remember):
- Watch for increased tail when cache evictions spike (pattern we saw in sim run C)
- Consider per-account cache caps later if multi-tenant noise shows up
- Keep messaging low-key for now — ops-focused, not product marketing

Slack channels / command references:
- #runtime-pilot (primary)
- /rollout status runtime-prefix-cache-v2 (console command to check)
- /rollback runtime-prefix-cache-v2 (manual kill)

Version history / local edits:
- 2025-02-12: initial outline
- 2025-02-16: added guardrails and schedule (Aisha)
- 2025-02-20: refined messaging and support template (Noelle)

End of draft — feedback wanted on: schedule timing, rollback thresholds, and support escalation wording.
